subject: english
chapter_title: The Case of the Fifth Word

concepts.title: Encyclopedia Brown, the Boy Detective
concepts.section: The Case of the Fifth Word, Let us read I
concepts.definition: Leroy Brown of Idaville, called Encyclopedia for his head full of facts, solves the police chief's hardest cases at the dinner table; he asks one careful question and never boasts about his help.
concepts.key_idea: Knowledge plus modesty makes the boy wonder: he reads endlessly, forgets nothing and keeps quiet about praise.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr103.txt, The Case of the Fifth Word, Let us read I
question_patterns: why is leroy brown called encyclopedia
how does encyclopedia help his father solve cases
what are the character traits of encyclopedia brown
why does chief brown keep his son's talent secret
what question does encyclopedia ask about the fir tree
how does encyclopedia find the meaning of the four words

solution_steps.explain: List what the character does and says at key moments.
Match each action to a quality such as wit, valour or patience.
Point to the lines of the text that support each trait.

concepts.title: The Four-Word Code: Nom Utes Sweden Hurts
concepts.section: The Case of the Fifth Word, Let us read II
concepts.definition: Dying, Tim Nolan leaves four strange words beside his will; Encyclopedia sees they hide the days of the week without the letters day, so the missing fifth word, fir for Friday, marks the young fir tree under which the stolen jewellery lies.
concepts.formula: nom utes sweden hurts = monday tuesday wednesday thursday
concepts.key_idea: A code bends around its calendar page: each word stands for a weekday, and the unwritten day points to the hiding place.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr103.txt, The Case of the Fifth Word, Let us read II
question_patterns: how did encyclopedia crack the four word code
what does nom stand for in nolan's code
why did nolan write the words on a calendar sheet
where was the stolen jewellery hidden
why would the code make no sense to a stranger
what was the fifth word and why was it left unwritten

solution_steps.explain: Write the four words exactly as Nolan left them.
Notice that dropping day from each weekday leaves letters that reshape into the words.
See that the fifth weekday gives fir, the tree under which the loot was buried.

concepts.title: Clues and Inference: Solving a Mystery
concepts.section: The Case of the Fifth Word, Let us think and reflect
concepts.definition: The story is a chain of clues, a five-year-old robbery, a missing partner, a searched house, a deathbed will; inference joins them, as Encyclopedia reasons from the calendar sheet and the single fir tree to the buried jug of earth.
concepts.key_idea: A detective reasons instead of guessing: each small fact, one question at a time, closes in on the answer.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr103.txt, The Case of the Fifth Word, Let us think and reflect
question_patterns: which clues help encyclopedia solve the case
why does encyclopedia ask about the fir tree in the nursery
what was suspicious about the sheet from the desk calendar
how did the police know that nolan and davenport hid the jewellery
why did the search of nolan's house find nothing
what does the case teach about careful reasoning

solution_steps.explain: Separate what is known, the robbery, the will, the searched house, from what is guessed.
Reason step by step from each clue towards the hiding place.
Test the answer against every clue before declaring the case closed.

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Hunch, Loot and Testify
concepts.section: The Case of the Fifth Word, Let us learn
concepts.definition: Detective words come clear from context: a hunch is a strong feeling about something, loot is stolen goods, to testify is to make a statement in court, and a hold-up is a robbery with threat or violence.
concepts.key_idea: Crime-story vocabulary, from court order to testimony, builds the world in which the boy detective works.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr103.txt, The Case of the Fifth Word, Let us learn

solution_steps.explain: Find the sentence where the new word appears.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How does the calendar sheet serve as the key to Nolan's code?

solution_template.explain: Nolan clipped a page from a desk calendar beside the will.
Once the words are read as weekdays missing their day letters, the unwritten fifth day, Fir or Friday, names the hiding spot.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why did Chief Brown stare at his soup at dinner?

solution_template.explain: Staring at the cream-of-mushroom soup was the chief's habit when a case defeated him.
Tim Nolan had died leaving a will and four words no one could read, and the stolen jewellery was still missing.
